source.title: Uncovering Safety Risks of Large Language Models through Concept Activation Vector
source.authors: Zhihao Xu; Ruixuan Huang; Changyu Chen; Xi-Ting Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates SCAV-guided attacks that deliberately alter embeddings or prompts to induce harmful responses. It does not test the specified fine-tuning, first-token KL, prefill, suffix/decoding, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The reported attack success and response rates are outcomes under attacks deliberately optimized to elicit harmful answers; they are not measurements of safety behavior without that inducement. The study does not report results for the claim versions. Detailed layer-sweep results in Figures 4 and 10 are figure-only and are not extracted as outcomes for any listed version.
record.test_reason: An attack-method paper. SCAV steers embeddings along a linear-probe direction, or optimizes AutoDAN-style prompts, to induce harmful answers. All reported numbers are the success rates of its own method or comparisons with baselines. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no per-token KL (V3), and no prefill or opening-token analysis (V4). It localizes nothing to weights or ranks (V5), gives no cause of shallowness (V6), and tests no deepening training (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SCAV enables effective embedding- and prompt-level attacks, that LLM safety risks are serious, and that better defenses are urgently needed. They also offer insights into layer-wise linear safety mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains linear safety-concept classifiers and uses them to optimize embedding perturbations and adversarial prompts; it does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that attack outcomes depend on layers perturbed: a perturbation at layer 0 does not improve ASR-keyword, while attacks at layers 10, 20, and 30 increase it; its discussion says multiple-layer perturbation is needed for high ASR. Results also vary across models and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful and safe instructions are linearly separable from about layer 10 in aligned models (over 95% probe accuracy) but not in unaligned Alpaca (Fig. 1, 7–9). Single-layer perturbation is corrected by later layers, while perturbing layers 10–13 jointly defeats safety (Fig. 4b, 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety in aligned LLMs is linearly represented in mid-to-late layers, and several layers must be steered jointly to bypass refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: SCAV embedding attacks induce harmful answers from seven open models, and transferred prompts do so from GPT-4 (Tables 5–6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-guided activation or prompt attacks can induce harmful compliance across aligned chat models.

record.problems: The reported harmful-response outcomes are attack-induced and do not establish rates of unprompted compliance. The authors note limited understanding of attack transferability. Main outcome tables do not give uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: Comparative baseline attack results, supplementary attack datasets/models, and detailed layer-sweep results were not extracted. They concern performance of the paper's attack methods rather than a listed claim version; some layer sweeps are figure-only. See Tables 1-4, 7, 15-18 and Figures 4, 10-14.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-position KL between aligned and base models.
Prefill of compliant openings, suffixes and decoding changes. GCG appears only as a baseline for the authors' method (Table 3).
Localization of safety to a small set of weights or ranks. The study perturbs activations, not parameters.
Data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
Deepening training. Circuit-breaker (RR) models are attacked in Table 18, but no token-depth augmentation is tested.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are the authors' own attack performance, so 'none' links and cannot_determine states are appropriate. The layer findings concern activations, not weights, so they do not bear on V5. Table 7 (Eraser) and Table 18 (circuit breakers) are attacks on defended models, not tests of V7's token-depth deepening.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling compliant opening tokens, suffix attacks, or decoding changes. The paper's SCAV prompt and embedding attacks are different interventions.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior. The paper perturbs activations at layers; it does not localize behavior to a small weight or rank set.
Whether training data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training to deepen safety and testing whether the effect persists.
